# Exercise 1

Using pandas and `penguins.csv`: select the Gentoo penguins with body mass above 5000 g keeping `species`, `island`, and `body_mass_g`, add a `body_mass_kg` column, and calculate the mean bill length and count for each species and island as a flat table.

```{python}
penguins = pd.read_csv("../data/penguins.csv")
```

```{python}
gentoo = penguins.loc[
  (penguins["species"] == "Gentoo") & (penguins["body_mass_g"] > 5000),
  ["species", "island", "body_mass_g"]
]
gentoo.head()
gentoo.shape
```

```{python}
penguins = penguins.assign(body_mass_kg = pd.col("body_mass_g") / 1000)
penguins.head()
```

```{python}
(penguins
  .groupby(["species", "island"], as_index=False)
  .agg(
    bill_length = ("bill_length_mm", "mean"),
    n = ("species", "size")
  )
)
```


# Exercise 2

Using polars: repeat the three tasks from Exercise 1, then rewrite part 3 to start from `pl.scan_csv()` and look at `explain()` before collecting.

```{python}
penguins = pl.read_csv("../data/penguins.csv", null_values="NA")
```

```{python}
penguins.filter(
  pl.col("species") == "Gentoo",
  pl.col("body_mass_g") > 5000
).select("species", "island", "body_mass_g")
```

```{python}
penguins = penguins.with_columns(body_mass_kg = pl.col("body_mass_g") / 1000)
penguins.head()
```

```{python}
penguins.group_by("species", "island").agg(
  bill_length = pl.col("bill_length_mm").mean(),
  n = pl.len()
).sort("species", "island")
```

```{python}
q = (
  pl.scan_csv("../data/penguins.csv", null_values="NA")
  .group_by("species", "island")
  .agg(
    bill_length = pl.col("bill_length_mm").mean(),
    n = pl.len()
  )
  .sort("species", "island")
)
print( q.explain() )  # PROJECT 3/8 COLUMNS
q.collect()
```
